claim.markdown_says: # 4.4 THE OPEN STATEMENT ... ## 4.4.1 Function ... ## 4.4.2 General Format ... ## 4.4.3 Syntax Rules ... ## 4.4.4 General Rules
claim.why_it_matters: Headings at the wrong level: the sibling sections 4.2 CLOSE and 4.3 DELETE (pages 447, 449) are '##' with '###' subsections, but 4.4 is promoted to a level-1 heading and its 4.4.x subsections to level 2, so a heading-based index puts OPEN at chapter level, outside section 4.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page VIII-21 (PDF p451) shows 4.4 THE OPEN STATEMENT with subsections 4.4.1-4.4.4 in the same typography as 4.2 CLOSE and 4.3 DELETE. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md, page 447 has '## 4.2 THE CLOSE STATEMENT' with '### 4.2.x', page 449 has '## 4.3 THE DELETE STATEMENT' with '### 4.3.x', and the chapter heading on page 446 is '## 4. PROCEDURE DIVISION IN THE RELATIVE I-O MODULE'; page 451 has '# 4.4 THE OPEN STATEMENT' and '## 4.4.1'-'## 4.4.4'. The text is all present; the defect is heading level only. 4.4 sits one level above its siblings and even above its own chapter heading, and 4.4.x sits at the siblings' section level. That breaks any heading-based structure of the document. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The kind is 'missing-heading', but the headings are present at the wrong level.
verdict.corrected_description: Not missing: the headings are present at the wrong markdown level. '# 4.4 THE OPEN STATEMENT' should be '## 4.4' and '## 4.4.1'-'## 4.4.4' should be '###', to match 4.2 CLOSE and 4.3 DELETE (pp. 447, 449) under the '## 4.' chapter heading on p. 446.
